$comment: The source of sf-tree-item's element plumbing (core/js/element-manifest.js). Taken from simai/ui-control control/smart-architecture/migration/out/tree-item (migration/convert-1.3.8.mjs over simai/ui-source@5100227); standard simai.smart-component 1.3.8, vocabulary 1.1.5. Every x-todo of the conversion is decided: x-decisions says how.

label.summary: The node's name; without it the node's own text is

value.summary: The node's id: data-value of its row, the id its events carry

items-data.summary: The node's children as data (sf-tree's entry shape); children written inside are read once otherwise

icon.summary: false hides the folder or file icon

open-label.summary: The chevron's name while the branch is closed

close-label.summary: The chevron's name while the branch is open

active.summary: The node is the current page: aria-current

open.summary: A press on the name, or Enter on a leaf without a link: open {id} of vocabulary 1.1.5 §5

toggle.summary: The branch opened or closed (vocabulary §5 toggle); the DOM name sf-tree-item-toggle is unchanged

expand.summary: Opens the branch; refused for a file, a leaf or a disabled node

toggle-open.summary: Opens a closed branch, closes an open one

activate.summary: What Enter does on a leaf: follows its link, or sends open

focus-item.summary: Moves the focus to the node's row

default.$comment: The Lit template in JavaScript, the migration form of §5.2 (§16). The row itself is js/templates/row.js, which sf-tree draws every entry with.

accessibility.$comment: The row is role treeitem with aria-expanded on a branch, aria-selected where the tree selects, aria-current for the current page; the chevron is a button named by open-label or close-label. Inside an sf-tree the tree draws the rows and owns the keys; a standalone node answers Enter on its name.

x-summary: A node of a tree: a folder that opens a group of nodes, or a file or link. Inside sf-tree it is read once as data and the tree draws its row; alone it draws itself.
x-renamed: settings.text → label: one name for the node's name; text is a dated setting alias
settings.type → kind: the legacy axis name (contracts/public-api-axes.json); a dated setting alias

events.sf-tree-item-click {item, value, originalEvent} → open {id, value}: "click" is a prototype name (§3.1) and the request is the vocabulary's open (§5); sf-tree-item-open, the old name a dated split alias
events.sf-tree-item-toggle {item, open, value} → toggle {id, open, value}: the DOM name is unchanged; the element left the detail (§8, data only) -- event.target is the node
methods open(), close(), toggle() → actions expand, collapse, toggle-open answering outcomes: open is the branch's value (§4), a property, and cannot also be a method

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-tree-item only as a node owned by sf-tree or a nested tree group.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not use a standalone tree item as a generic list row
Do not move host data or access decisions into the component

x-decisions: rows (simai/ui-source#43, §18.4): the row is class markup drawn by js/templates/row.js -- icons are the icon font's <i class="sf-icon">, not sf-icon elements -- and sf-tree draws every entry with the same function. Inside an sf-tree the node is read once as data and removed (as before); the tree does not draw sf-tree-item elements any more. Alone, the node draws its row and, open, its children as nested sf-tree-item elements.

events (vocabulary 1.1.5 §5): a press on the name, or Enter on a leaf without a link, asks to open the node: sf-tree-item-open {id, value}; sf-tree-item-click follows until 2026-12-01 as a split alias whose adapter gives {item, value, originalEvent: null}. The branch's change keeps its DOM name sf-tree-item-toggle with {id, open, value}; the element left the detail (§8: data only), event.target is the node.

actions: expand, collapse and toggle-open answer outcomes ({outcome: refused, reason: leaf | disabled} for a node that cannot open); activate follows the link or sends open; focus-item focuses the row. The old open()/close()/toggle() methods are gone: open is the branch's value and a property (§4); they returned the element for chaining and nothing outside the tree called them.

item-shape: items-data is a list of entries named with of (sf-tree's entry shape: id, label, href, target, rel, kind, value, open, selected, active, disabled, icon, the four icons, the two chevron names, revision, children), keyed by id with changes: content (§18.4). The camelCase fields (openIcon, …) and type are still read.
text and type leave the settings: text is label's dated alias, type kind's (aliases.json).
open-label and close-label default to the language files' runtime words (default-from); TREE_ITEM_TEXT is gone.
key-effects: a standalone node answers Enter on its name (open) and Tab reaches its row; the arrows, Home, End and Space are the tree's (sf-tree's keyboard), which owns the roving tab stop.
version 1.1.0: members renamed behind dated aliases (§4.10); the methods' retirement is recorded in x-renamed.
template: templates.default names the Lit template js/templates/default.js; the row is js/templates/row.js.
examples: examples.json from studio.fixture.json (a section with a child) plus a file, a link, a disabled node and a node without an icon.

css-variables: five public variables of the tree-item class sheet (component/tree-item): the line's gap, the name's ink (outside a tree; inside, the name takes the row's colour), the icons' ink, and a drop target's fill and ring. Listed in src/core/contracts/public-variables.v1.json.
source-drift: the shipped manifest differs from 5100227 in its provenance hashes and the rule's relation names; the interface is the same, nothing to carry.

version 1.1.1: the first-paint snapshots are retaken: the JSON island is printed once (no held copy), the icon font's state (sf-icon loaded, sf-icon-loaded) is left out, a closed surface prints closed and a size or place the code measured (a non-zero px width, height, inset, clip or transform) is left out, so a snapshot is the same on every run.

version 1.1.2: the bundle carries no element layer of its own -- element-manifest, aliases, the alias table, the host port, deprecations, page actions, the layer stack, the open-surface mark and the instance path come from the page's shared runtime (SF.runtimeModule, runtime ABI 1, core.runtime 1.1.0), one instance per page -- and embeds of this file only the keys the runtime reads. Behaviour unchanged.
